elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose third-party commercial offers to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor any commercial offer received from another provider.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match, extend, or otherwise provide Vendor the benefit of more favourable third-party commercial terms.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer has no obligation to match for Vendor any commercial offer received from another provider; Section 12.3 also confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered clause eliminates the MFN obligation entirely, so no MFN can apply beyond a defined product.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Customer has no MFN obligation, so none can continue beyond 12 months.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it includes reasonable-comparison carve-outs so that only reasonably comparable offers or transactions are compared.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: no offer is subject to an MFN comparison because Section 7.2 disclaims both disclosure and matching obligations.

result.reason: The operative redline completely removes the Customer-burdening disclosure and matching duties and aligns Section 7.2 with the existing no-MFN statement in Section 12.3. It therefore satisfies the preferred position. It also necessarily satisfies the fallback limitations because no MFN obligation remains to exceed the product, duration, or comparability limits. The change is targeted, clear, and does not alter unrelated commercial terms.
